subtopic: Responding to a natural disaster or accident
subtype: Approach: following a practised emergency plan [Action]
passage:
“Bhavna, the shaking has stopped but the building is still creaking. Do the list,” Papa called from the stairwell.
“Bag first.” Bhavna pulled the emergency bag from behind the shoe rack. “Documents folder, torch, water bottles, Mummy's spectacles. Got them.”
“Didi, my shoes are under the bed!”
“I'll grab them. Papa, the mains?”
“Off at the big switch, then the gas knob. Left side, the red one.”
“Done. Gas is off too.”
“Good. Meeting point is the school gate, not the lift, not the parking lot.”
“I know. Mr Sen's drill, remember? Aadhya, hold my hand, we take the stairs.”
They went down together, the torch beam bouncing on the steps, and at the gate Mummy was already waving both arms.

qa.q: Which things did Bhavna list from the emergency bag?
qa.a: She named a documents folder, a torch, water bottles and Mummy's spectacles.

qa.q: What does Bhavna's steady list suggest she is feeling?
qa.a: She seems calm and focused, though probably a bit tense, and her quick replies show she trusts the practised plan.

qa.q: What could the family do if the stairs were blocked, and why?
qa.a: They could use the second agreed way out or wait for adult rescue guidance, because a plan with a backup route stops panic when the first choice fails.

qa.q: How might Aadhya feel about the plan?
qa.a: Aadhya may be frightened, but holding Didi's hand and hearing clear instructions makes it feel manageable.

grounding: A teen uses a family plan practised in school drills: takes the emergency bag, switches off the mains as an adult says, and goes to the meeting point.

subtopic: Responding to a natural disaster or accident
subtype: Approach: following a practised emergency plan [Action]
passage:
The fire alarm in our building went off at 9:40 one night last year. I'm Manoj, and the only reason I didn't freeze is that we had practised this exact thing at home after the school drill in June.
Papa shouted from the balcony, “Smoke from the floor below. Plan!” My part of the plan was simple, because we'd said it out loud so many times. I grabbed the red bag from behind the door: our documents in a plastic folder, the torch, water, Papa's tablets. Papa told me to switch off the mains, and I did it at the switch box by the kitchen, just as we'd practised, only because he said to. We took the stairs, not the lift, Mummy holding my sister's hand.
The meeting point was the gate by the temple. Baljeet's family was already there. We counted: four of us. Everyone.
The fire was small in the end. But my hands only stopped shaking when I counted four.

qa.q: What was in the red bag?
qa.a: The documents in a plastic folder, the torch, water and Papa's tablets.

qa.q: What was Manoj feeling until the family was counted at the gate?
qa.a: Manoj was frightened, hands shaking, and only felt relief after counting all four of them.

qa.q: What else could the family add to the plan after this night?
qa.a: Practise it together again and check the red bag every few months, so everything inside is still there and up to date.

qa.q: How might Baljeet's family have seen Manoj's family arrive?
qa.a: They would likely be relieved to see all four safe at the gate, and glad both families knew the same meeting point.

grounding: Shows a teen following a family plan practised after school drills: taking the emergency bag, switching off the mains when told, and going to the meeting point.

Parent's note for the school's safety week display
When the landslide siren sounded in our village above Munnar on Saturday night, I watched our son Jomon do exactly what his school had drilled. He took the green emergency bag from the hook without being told: the documents pouch, the torch, the whistle, dry biscuits. I asked him to switch off the mains at the board by the door, and he did, then checked the gas knob too, as we had shown him. He held his sister Rajni's hand and walked with her down the path to the church hall, the meeting point we had agreed after the June drill.
At the hall he counted us and told the volunteer our names and how many we were. The slope held that night, and we went home the next afternoon.
I am writing this because I was the one shaking. He was calm, because he had practised.

qa.q: Where was the agreed meeting point?
How did Jomon seem during the evacuation, according to the note?
qa.a: Jomon seemed calm and steady because he had practised, while the parent was the one shaking.

qa.q: What else could the family practise before the next monsoon?
qa.a: Walking the path to the church hall at night with the torch, so the route feels familiar even in dark and rain.

qa.q: What was it like for Rajni to walk down with Jomon?
qa.a: Rajni had a steady hand to hold and someone who knew the way, which probably made a frightening night feel safer.

grounding: A parent notes a teen following a practised plan: taking the emergency bag, switching off the mains when asked, and going to the agreed meeting point.
